question: A chat UI renders markdown. Why is an image more dangerous than a link in model output?
options: The browser fetches the image as soon as the answer renders, so data in its URL leaves without any user action; a link needs a click
explanation: Zero-click is what makes image exfiltration so effective. Links still matter (users click convincing ones), which is why both are checked.

question: A filter allows URLs when `url.includes('docs.example.com')`. Which URL defeats it?
explanation: Substring checks match the attacker's subdomain. Parse the URL and compare the normalized hostname exactly; `https://docs.example.com@attacker.example/` is another classic, where the allowed name is only the username.

question: Your allowlist contains your own domain, which has an open redirect at `/go?to=`. What does that mean?
options: Nothing: the allowlist only checks the first hop
The allowed host becomes a channel: an image or link through the redirect can still reach the attacker, so fix the redirect or remove the host from the allowlist
Only links are affected, never images
explanation: EchoLeak used an allowlisted Microsoft domain that proxied requests. Every host on the allowlist must be reviewed for redirects, proxies and user-controlled content.

question: A customer name from the model, `" onfocus="alert(1)`, is inserted into `<input value="...">` after HTML text encoding (`&`, `<`, `>`). What goes wrong?
options: The double quote is not encoded, so it closes the attribute and adds an event handler; attributes need quotes encoded too
explanation: Each destination needs its own encoding. HTML attribute context must also escape `"` and `'`; URLs need `encodeURIComponent`; SQL and shells need parameters.

question: Why keep a Content Security Policy when the sanitizer already removes non-allowlisted images?
options: CSP replaces the sanitizer, so the sanitizer can be deleted
Defense in depth: if the sanitizer misses a construct (a new markdown syntax, a renderer quirk), the browser still refuses to load resources from hosts outside `img-src` and `connect-src`
explanation: Sanitizers have bugs and renderers evolve. A browser-enforced policy is an independent layer that does not depend on your parsing being perfect.
